metadata.goal: Analyze how different vessel movements interact in the waters east of Møn and how their navigation changes across different traffic conditions.
metadata.category: mixed traffic interactions east of møn
metadata.header: Mixed traffic interactions east of Møn
metadata.dataset_description: Constructed cargo, tanker, ferry, and Tourist vessel movements in open water east of Møn, including repeated crossings and varied crossing-traffic conditions.
metadata.source_note: Danish maritime geography is used as context; the visible trajectories and attributes are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Cargo and tanker vessels mainly follow stable through-traffic paths, while ferry vessels repeatedly cross these flows and tourist vessels show more dispersed movements across the area.

plot.title: Mixed Traffic East of Møn
plot.description: Compare stable through traffic, repeated ferry crossings, and dispersed tourist-vessel excursions.

insight_list.question: How do vessel movement roles differ east of Møn?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare stable through traffic, repeated ferry crossings, and dispersed tourist-vessel excursions.

insight_list.insight: Repeated ferry vessel crossings typically contain a short phase of reduced speed and increased COG variation near the main traffic flow, followed by a return to more stable movement after the crossing.

plot.title: Ferry Crossing Dynamics
plot.description: Compare speed and successive COG variation inside and outside the crossing-interaction phase.

insight_list.question: How do ferry movements change while crossing the main traffic flow?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare speed and successive COG variation inside and outside the crossing-interaction phase.

insight_list.insight: Through-traffic vessels show more frequent short-term speed and course adjustments during periods with heavier crossing traffic, while their movement remains more stable when crossing activity is sparse.

plot.title: Through-traffic Adjustments by Crossing Activity
plot.description: Classify traffic using concurrent crossing-vessel rates, then compare individual trajectories and group distributions.

insight_list.question: How does crossing activity affect through-traffic stability?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Classify traffic using concurrent crossing-vessel rates, then compare individual trajectories and group distributions.

insights: Cargo and tanker vessels mainly follow stable through-traffic paths, while ferry vessels repeatedly cross these flows and tourist vessels show more dispersed movements across the area.

Repeated ferry vessel crossings typically contain a short phase of reduced speed and increased COG variation near the main traffic flow, followed by a return to more stable movement after the crossing.

Through-traffic vessels show more frequent short-term speed and course adjustments during periods with heavier crossing traffic, while their movement remains more stable when crossing activity is sparse.
summary: Cargo and tanker vessels mainly follow stable through-traffic paths, while ferry vessels repeatedly cross these flows and tourist vessels show more dispersed movements across the area. Repeated ferry vessel crossings typically contain a short phase of reduced speed and increased COG variation near the main traffic flow, followed by a return to more stable movement after the crossing. Through-traffic vessels show more frequent short-term speed and course adjustments during periods with heavier crossing traffic, while their movement remains more stable when crossing activity is sparse.
